description: A reversal must be recognisable AS a reversal in the sheets an auditor reads, not only in the export. The journal has carried `reverses`/`reversedBy` since the beginning and `journalExport` publishes both, but `cashJournal` and `accountSheet` showed a reversal as an ordinary opposite movement: a reader saw +100.00 and −100.00 and could not tell whether a mistake was corrected or a genuine receipt was removed. That distinction is exactly what a formal audit turns on (BFH 29.07.2025, X R 23/21 and X R 24/21: a system that permits cancellations without showing them in its output is formally defective, and no proof of manipulation is required for that to matter). Both projections now carry `reversesEntry` on the reversing movement and `reversedByEntry` on the reversed one — journal sequence numbers rather than UUIDs, because these two views are read by a person who looks the counterpart up by its number. Substrate, not pack: the traceability of a correction is mechanism, and it holds in every jurisdiction. One detail makes the gap worse than it sounds: this core reverses by *general reversal* — EntryLine::negated keeps the side and negates the amount — so a reversed cash receipt appears in the cash book as a debit of −100.00, not as a credit. Without a marker a reader sees a negative amount on the debit side and has nothing telling them why.

movements.comment: Die stornierte Buchung nennt ihre Stornobuchung — ohne das ist nicht erkennbar, dass sie aufgehoben wurde
Generalumkehr: gleiche Seite, negativer Betrag. Die Stornobuchung nennt die Buchung, die sie aufhebt — genau die Angabe, deren Fehlen den formellen Mangel ausmacht
